title: Climate benefit and ecological cost trade-offs for ocean iron fertilization.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the Zenodo deposit (record 20500155, CC-BY-4.0, published 2026-06-02) via the Zenodo API: two files, CODE_DATA.zip at 2,373,720,159 bytes (~2.4 GB, over the 50 MB cap, not downloaded) and a 1.8 kB README.txt, which I read. The README says the archive holds Python and NCL (NCAR Command Language) plotting scripts plus the CESM2-8P4Z model output needed to redraw each figure.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything else comes from the abstract only (no PMC full text): a single ocean biogeochemistry simulation model (CESM2-8P4Z) run under fertilization scenarios across ten ocean biomes for 60 years, with outputs such as carbon removal, oxygen-minimum-zone extent and zooplankton biomass. No row counts, variables or file formats inside the zip were seen.

a1_downloadable.note: Open Zenodo record with no login, CC-BY-4.0; the single data file is a 2.4 GB zip (checked via the API, not downloaded).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table of labelled examples. The outputs are gridded simulation fields organised by figure, and any target would have to be built from them. Judged from the README, not from opening the zip.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs for each 'example' would be the scenario settings (biome, fertilization on or off) of one model. These are a handful of experiment conditions, not per-item features.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked. NetCDF climate-model output normally carries units attributes, but I did not open the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 10 biome scenarios plus global and recovery runs, per the abstract. Grid cells and time steps from one simulation are autocorrelated, not independent examples.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2.4 GB zip (size verified via the API)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Fits on disk and in memory if subset, but it is over the 50 MB download cap, so it was not fetched.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable: neither the paper text nor the zip contents were seen.

a8_label_provenance.note: Every candidate label (carbon removal, oxygen-minimum-zone volume, macrozooplankton biomass) is the output of the CESM2-8P4Z simulation, computed from that model's own inputs. Any ML model would just imitate this one model run (a surrogate), not learn from a physical measurement.

backbone.name: none: no biological sequence, molecule or single-cell data

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here could only claim to imitate how one climate-model configuration (CESM2-8P4Z) responds to a few iron-fertilization scenarios. It would say nothing measured about the real ocean.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the region and settings of an ocean iron-fertilization scenario to predict the simulated carbon removal and ecosystem damage.
plain_idea.train_on: Scenario settings (which of 10 ocean biomes is fertilized, and for how long) and gridded fields from one ocean simulation model. Number of independent examples is unknown but roughly a dozen scenarios.
plain_idea.predict: Simulated carbon removed and simulated changes in oxygen-poor zones and zooplankton. All of these are outputs of the same computer model, not field measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: A fast stand-in for the simulation could help ocean-carbon-removal policy groups screen regions. But with about a dozen scenarios from one model, it would only reproduce that model's results.

ml_idea: Considered: a surrogate (fast stand-in) model of CESM2-8P4Z fertilization responses. Rejected because the labels are simulation outputs (A8), there are only about a dozen scenarios (A5), and there is no labelled table (A2).

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project was rejected at Part A. The only verified figure is the 2.4 GB size of the zip, read from the Zenodo API.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the README to see what the deposit contains: it showed figure-level simulation output from one model, which already kills the project.

verdict_reason: The deposit is ~2.4 GB of output from one ocean simulation model (CESM2-8P4Z), packed by figure. Every possible label is a simulation result (A8 failure), there are only about a dozen scenarios (A5), and there is no labelled table (A2).
